claims.statement: North Carolina homeowners underwriting uses a three-layer boundary: the appetite guide and Rule 550 are internal eligibility, referral, evidence, and authority controls; NCDOI-2018-03 and NCDOI-2021-06 govern disclosure and claims administration; and HO 01 32 controls only the contract provisions it changes when attached.

The NC internal appetite permits Coverage A from $150,000 through $1,000,000, requires a roof inspection before binding at roof age 18 years or greater, requires a wind-mitigation inspection when Coverage A exceeds $500,000, and refers two paid property claims in the preceding three-year review.

NC delegated authority permits binding Coverage A up to $700,000 only when the risk otherwise fits the approved appetite; requests above that amount must be referred before terms are offered, and the exposure must not be split or restructured to evade referral.

NC roof underwriting requires current, supportable evidence of age, material, condition, repairs, and serviceability, and requires referral or hold for leakage, deterioration, structural distress, defective details, unresolved storm damage, obscured condition, or unsupported future repair; an internal roof rule is not a claim-settlement exclusion.

NC water-risk review begins with the physical source and path and requires referral or hold for active or recurring water conditions, unresolved moisture, drainage or below-grade entry, defective plumbing or protective devices, and incomplete remediation; water-backup eligibility and limits must be taken from the actual endorsement and declarations rather than from an internal referral rule.

For an attached HO 01 32, the contractual windstorm-and-hail deductible applies only to covered loss directly caused by windstorm or hail and is between 1% and 5%; an increase requires written notice at least 30 days before its effective date, and a Named Storm Period or Seacoast Territory does not itself create coverage.

The NC loss-history control reviews the preceding three years and refers two paid property claims, but also requires evaluation of cause, recurrence, repair quality, mitigation, current condition, discrepancies, and unresolved hazards rather than relying on claim count alone.

The internal NC claims handoff opens and documents the claim promptly, verifies the policy package, protects property, uses a seven-day-after-discovery mitigation checkpoint and a 60-day suspected-water-backup intake target when practicable, investigates cause and scope, requests relevant evidence, escalates complex or adverse matters, and closes only after known issues are resolved.

For the applicable NC contract and claims bulletin, claim receipt is acknowledged within 30 days, a claim is accepted or rejected within 30 business days after needed requested items are received, and an accepted claim is paid within 30 business days after payment becomes due; written decisions must identify relevant policy provisions and material facts.

NCDOI-2018-03 requires a clear, conspicuous, understandable, retainable fungi, wet-rot, dry-rot, or bacteria limitation disclosure, including the statement that the most the insurer will pay is $5,000, for applicable policy transactions; the disclosure must match the policy and cannot create or alter coverage.

When HO 01 32 is attached, its contract states a $5,000 maximum for all loss caused by fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria and requires express coverage for such loss; a fungi allegation or observation still requires reasonable investigation and a written, policy-based explanation before limitation or denial.

NCDOI-2021-06 keeps the insurer responsible for claims handled by employees, adjusters, producers, administrators, vendors, and other representatives and requires procedures, supervision, training, quality review, privacy controls, complaint escalation, and records sufficient to show the basis for material decisions.

A required NC referral remains on hold until authorized direction is recorded and conditions are satisfied; approval is risk- and term-specific, verbal assurance or silence is not approval, material changes require reassessment, and the underwriting file must retain the trigger, sources, authority, conditions, communications, and final disposition.

The NC underwriting record must distinguish reported from verified facts, record sources and dates, preserve discrepancies and adverse information even when a risk is accepted, document authority and referral reasons, and retain completion evidence before closing a corrective requirement.

North Carolina underwriting records must tie each material decision to the operative transaction package and preserve state-specific evidence: verify the North Carolina HO-3 policy/form position, effective date, and attached HO 01 32 (2018-05) when applicable; retain the matching fungi disclosure with delivery and filing or approval records; and preserve dated claim-handoff records and delegated-party oversight when a loss is routed.
